_comment: bits credentials proxy (M6): the second security-proxy instance, which holds the services' GitLab tokens and store keys so that the backend and the worker hold none. Copy to CREDENTIALS_PROXY_CONFIG_DIR as config.json (root-owned, read-only: a changed upstream would replay the tokens elsewhere). Every secret is an ingest slot pushed by `make unlock` (tools/service-secrets.py) and held only in memory; until then the routes answer 503. 'cert' is a throwaway self-signed client certificate generated and pushed at unlock: the proxy needs one to build its TLS client, and none of these upstreams asks for it. The GitLab routes are matched by the PRIVATE-TOKEN header (each client sends its gate token there, as it would a GitLab token) and told apart by the gate token, which is per route. The S3 route is matched by the AWS Authorization header; each bucket names its own keypair. The agent socket hands the gate token of EVERY route here to whoever can read it (the backend and the worker): keep only what they need. Same in-container socket paths as the signer's; they are different volumes.
